activity.notes: Imhotep was a historical non-royal adviser to King Djoser and is credited with the design/oversight of Djoser's Step Pyramid. Exact appointment boundaries are not preserved. ATLAS therefore uses Djoser's approximate 2667–2648 BCE reign only as a representative service window and marks both boundaries approximate rather than treating them as Imhotep's exact term.

sources.title: Imhotep — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum of Art identifies Imhotep as adviser to King Djoser in the Third Dynasty and credits him with the design of the Step Pyramid at Saqqara.

sources.title: The Step Pyramid Complex of Djoser — Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities
sources.citation_text: Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities dates Djoser's reign approximately 2667–2648 BCE and identifies the Step Pyramid as his Third Dynasty monument; this reign provides only a representative chronological envelope for Imhotep's service.
